memory_candidates.content: When verify-deploy.sh / tests/run-all.sh fails during a concurrent /orchestrate batch, check git status --short on the specific failing paths before treating the failure as your own regression: a doc-lint or manifest-driven content-drift finding on a file outside your own file_scope is very likely an uncommitted, unredeployed edit from a sibling task sharing the same working tree this cycle, not something you broke. Cross-reference the dispatch's Territory block's concurrent_siblings file_scope lists to confirm.

A Bash tool call for a slow verification script (verify-deploy.sh, tests/run-all.sh) reliably auto-backgrounds around 120-540s of wall-clock regardless of the requested timeout. The reliable pattern: launch via `nohup cmd > logfile 2>&1 & echo pid=$!` in one call, then in a follow-up call run a bounded `while kill -0 "$pid"; do sleep N; done` loop with an outer iteration cap, reading the log file directly for interim progress between polls rather than waiting idle.
